payload.goal:
Add exactly 4 independent warehouse analytics modules to the verified W1 codebase.
Create src/analytics/contracts.ts exporting WarehouseProjection with a readonly id and project(scenario), where project returns the answer to that module's question.
Each module answers one question, computed from the W1 Scenario, layout and inventory exports:
- src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports the projection "zone-unit-totals": Total units stored in each zone, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports the projection "sku-unit-totals": Total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports the projection "bin-occupancy": How many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports the projection "sku-bin-spread": Number of distinct bins each SKU occupies, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts.
A module must not import another module; it may import only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Every answer must be derived from the scenario at run time. Do not hardcode results, and do not duplicate the W1 inventory or layout calculations.
Create src/analytics/registry.ts as the sole consumer of every module, returning all projections in the order the modules are listed above, with its own tests in src/analytics/registry.test.ts.
Preserve all existing W1 behaviour and checks.
Add a package script named study:wide-graph that writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and no other output.
Its JSON must be { "schemaVersion": 1, "moduleCount": 4, "scenario": "thesis-seed-2026", "projections": [ { "projectionId": "<the module's projection id>", "value": <that module's answer> }, … ] } with exactly 4 entries in the order the modules are listed above.
Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical JSON.

root.title: Warehouse analytics modules
root.objective: Add four independent runtime warehouse analytics projections, their registry, and deterministic study output while preserving W1 behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Four projection modules compute answers from W1 scenario, layout, and inventory exports at run time.
A shared WarehouseProjection contract describes projection ids and project(scenario).
The registry is the sole internal consumer of the projection modules and preserves the required order.
The study:wide-graph package script emits one byte-stable JSON object with four ordered projection results.
Existing W1 tests and behavior remain covered.

complexitySignals.rationale: The work adds a new analytics area plus a package script, but relies on existing W1 exports and has narrow public surface.

cut.rationale: Each projection is a cohesive independently testable runtime calculation; the contract, registry, and command are separate integration concerns with distinct consumers and acceptance checks.

children.title: Projection contract
children.objective: Create src/analytics/contracts.ts exporting WarehouseProjection with readonly id and project(scenario).
expectedOutcomes: WarehouseProjection is exported from src/analytics/contracts.ts.
The contract exposes readonly id and project(scenario).
The project method is compatible with the W1 Scenario export without introducing module-level projection dependencies.

complexitySignals.rationale: Small new exported type, but it is consumed by every analytics module and registry.

children.title: Zone unit totals
children.objective: Implement projection-01 as zone-unit-totals, totaling stored units by zone id from the runtime scenario.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id "zone-unit-totals".
project(scenario) returns total units stored in each zone keyed by zone id.
The module imports only the analytics contract and W1 exports, not other analytics modules.
src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts verifies the projection from W1 scenario data rather than hardcoded duplicated W1 calculations.

complexitySignals.rationale: Single projection plus focused tests, requiring enough W1 layout and inventory context to map stock to zones.

children.title: SKU unit totals
children.objective: Implement projection-02 as sku-unit-totals, totaling units by SKU id across the runtime scenario.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id "sku-unit-totals".
project(scenario) returns total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse keyed by SKU id.
The module imports only the analytics contract and W1 exports, not other analytics modules.
src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts verifies whole-warehouse SKU totals from W1 scenario data.

complexitySignals.rationale: Single aggregation over inventory quantities with focused test surface.

children.title: Bin occupancy
children.objective: Implement projection-03 as bin-occupancy, reporting stocked, empty, and total bin counts from the runtime scenario.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id "bin-occupancy".
project(scenario) returns how many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist.
The module imports only the analytics contract and W1 exports, not other analytics modules.
src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts verifies occupied, empty, and total bin counts using W1 layout and inventory behavior.

complexitySignals.rationale: Requires integrating layout bin universe with inventory occupancy without duplicating W1 calculations.

children.title: SKU bin spread
children.objective: Implement projection-04 as sku-bin-spread, counting distinct occupied bins per SKU from the runtime scenario.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports a WarehouseProjection with id "sku-bin-spread".
project(scenario) returns the number of distinct bins each SKU occupies, keyed by SKU id.
The module imports only the analytics contract and W1 exports, not other analytics modules.
src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts verifies distinct-bin spread for each SKU from W1 scenario data.

complexitySignals.rationale: Single projection with distinctness semantics that need focused assertions.

children.title: Analytics registry
children.objective: Create src/analytics/registry.ts as the sole consumer of every projection module and return them in required order.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/registry.ts imports all four projection modules and returns all projections in the required order.
No non-registry analytics file imports another projection module.
src/analytics/registry.test.ts verifies module count, projection ids, order, and that registry outputs use the shared WarehouseProjection contract.

complexitySignals.rationale: Small exported integration point, but it enforces the sole-consumer and ordering requirements.

children.title: Study wide graph command
children.objective: Add the study:wide-graph package script and command implementation that emits exactly one deterministic JSON object.
expectedOutcomes: package.json includes a study:wide-graph script.
The command uses the analytics registry and thesis-seed-2026 scenario to emit exactly one JSON object and no other output.
The emitted JSON has schemaVersion 1, moduleCount 4, scenario "thesis-seed-2026", and four ordered projection entries matching registry order.
Two invocations from the same commit produce byte-identical output.
The package test configuration includes the new analytics tests while preserving existing W1 checks.

complexitySignals.rationale: Touches package command surface and test coverage, consumes registry output, and must preserve byte-stable stdout behavior.
